title: A negative solution to the finite lattice representation problem
main_claim: There is a finite lattice that is not the full congruence lattice of any finite algebra. The paper proves this by building a self-dual finite lattice (a Boolean B4 plus a "detector", decorated with long tested chains) that is not an interval [D,G] in the subgroup lattice of any finite group, and then applying the Palfy-Pudlak global equivalence.

issues.location: sections/classification.tex, Theorem cls:chain-rigidity, proved through sections/growth.tex, lifts.tex, packets.tex and rigidity.tex
issues.description: Not a demonstrated gap, but a limit on this review. The whole result depends on the uniform chain-rigidity theorem: a tested chain of length at least an absolute B has equal endpoint simple types. Its proof runs about 4000 lines and leans heavily on the classification of finite simple groups (Aschbacher classes, Larsen-Pink envelopes, Landazuri-Seitz bounds, the Burness-Testerman irreducible-triple tables, Steinberg/Lubeck). I checked the reduction lemmas and the final rigidity argument and found them internally consistent. These include the bounded-rank prime-subfield Omega argument, index multiplicativity e_ik = e_ij e_jk, the constituent-count lemma, the Ramsey and rank-set argument with |R(r)| <= 7, and the quadratic-versus-polynomial growth contradiction. I did not verify the growth catalogue, the algebraic path lifts, or the packet composition-length theorem line by line.
issues.evidence: 'There is an absolute integer B such that every tested chain of length N >= B satisfies T_a ≅ T_b.' The proof is completed in Section rigidity using Prop. grw:remaining-paths and Thm pkt:bounded-length.

issues.location: sections/classification.tex, Prop. cls:literature (L4), (L5); Lemma cls:alternating; Lemma cls:uniform-actions(i)
issues.description: Two load-bearing external inputs are used as black boxes and could not be checked here. (L4): a second maximal subgroup of an almost simple group has at most five nonabelian chief factors (Burness-Liebeck-Shalev 2017, Prop 8.1). (L5): a height-two interval in an alternating or symmetric group has at most 11 interior vertices (Basile's 2001 PhD thesis, Theorem D; the bib key says 2008). The M16 test and the five-chief-factor bound on H_* rely entirely on these statements, with the exact hypotheses quoted. If either is misquoted, the type-pool and alternating-exclusion steps fail.
issues.evidence: 'If [H,A] is a height-two interval and A is alternating or symmetric of degree at least five, it has at most eleven interior vertices [Basile2008, Theorem D]'
